svg.title: How the assistant reads the text of an issue
svg.desc: The text of an issue or a comment, which anyone can write, is read up to GitHub's 65,536 characters. The answers of a form are cut out between their headings, which are found once; from them come the labels of the form and the reporter's language. For the AI, the HTML goes first, comments and tags in one pass, then the link reference definitions and the footnotes without a reference, which GitHub shows as nothing as well, each with a note in its place, for issue.md and for an excerpt of each other issue, whose form answers then become lines. Then the characters that GitHub shows as nothing go, in one pass, after the HTML, so that none can end an HTML comment that GitHub never ends. The excerpts go into issues.jsonl, and issue.md holds up to 20,000 characters of each text in a code fence that the text can't close.
